title: IA generativa: escribiendo, editando y diseñando en 2023
summary: El 2023 está siendo un año clave para la inteligencia artificial (IA), particularmente para los softwares que utilizan IA generativa - fundamentados en modelos de aprendizaje avanzados que facilitan la generación de imágenes, textos y códigos de programación, entre otros contenidos. body_text: El 2023 está siendo un año clave para la inteligencia artificial (IA), particularmente para los softwares que utilizan IA generativa - fundamentados en modelos de aprendizaje avanzados que facilitan la generación de imágenes, textos y códigos de programación, entre otros contenidos. Podíamos decir que esta categoría de IA está transformando la forma en que realizamos diversas tareas. La organización de investigación OpenAI ha sido fundamental en popularizar la IA generativa, un tema que analizamos en profundidad aquí . En septiembre de 2023, la web de la organización registró 102,8 millones de visitantes únicos, lo que representa un aumento del 127% desde enero del mismo año. Tanto la herramienta de diseño digital de OpenAI, DALL.E , como su generador de texto y código de programación, ChatGPT , han fomentado que los usuarios experimenten con ellas y compartan sus creaciones en las redes sociales. Por ejemplo, hemos visto al influencer de Microsoft, Mike Tholfsen, compartiendo cómo aprovechar ChatGPT en la creación de presentaciones de Power Point, o a la influencer Karen X editando un mismo prompt con DALL.E para obtener diversos resultados de diseño, entre otros. @mtholfsen Use ChatGPT to automate creating a #PowerPoint deck These are just simple ideas to get you started - have fun! #PPT #powerpointnight #learnontiktok #chatgpt #ai #officetips #Microsoft #hacks Monkeys Spinning Monkeys - Kevin MacLeod & Kevin The Monkey @karenxcheng I made a “music video” using AI to generate all images - using DALL-E 2 #dalle2 #artificialintelligence Feeling Good - Nina Simone Fuente: Comscore Social, Content Pulse, contenido que menciona “ChatGPT” o “DALL.E”, en TikTok, 2022-2023 Con el creciente interés público en esta tecnología, plataformas basadas en IA generativa como Character.ai y Wondershare.com han ganado popularidad y han mejorado durante 2023. Character.ai está redefiniendo el diseño de chatbots y avatares, mientras que Wondershare ha mejorado en la edición de videos y presentaciones. Para comprender mejor el impacto global de la IA de estas plataformas, nos centraremos en los datos de ocho países. En septiembre de 2023, la audiencia estadounidense de Character.ai superó los 2 millones de visitantes únicos. En México, la cifra se acercó al medio millón, seguida por la audiencia del Reino Unido, Brasil, Francia, España, India e Italia, en ese orden. El análisis de afinidad de esta plataforma muestra las tendencias de los visitantes únicos por rango de edad y país. Los adultos de la Generación Z ocupan los primeros puestos en el índice en casi todos los países, especialmente en Italia, donde aquellos de 18-24 años registraron un impresionante 597 en el índice de composición de visitantes únicos* en septiembre de 2023, es decir, 5.97 veces mayor que su representación en la población digital total del país. España es la excepción, donde la audiencia de 25-34 años es 4.42 veces mayor (índice de composición UV* = 442). En cuanto a la audiencia de Wondershare.com , esta otra plataforma impulsada por IA registró más de 7 millones de visitantes únicos durante septiembre de 2023. Estados Unidos y Brasil también alcanzaron las siete cifras, con 3 millones y 1 millón de visitantes únicos respectivamente. El Reino Unido también logró una audiencia considerable, superando el medio millón de visitantes únicos mensuales durante el mismo periodo. En el análisis de afinidad de Wondershare destaca la popularidad de la plataforma entre los adultos de la Generación Z en Estados Unidos, cuyo índice de composición de UV es 268. Aunque en menor medida, también se observa en los jóvenes de 18-24 años de Francia (150), España (148), México (147) y la India (136). En el grupo de edad de 25-34 años, la plataforma tiene un uso significativo en España (194), Brasil (159), Estados Unidos (158), Italia (128) y Francia (107). Curiosamente, esta plataforma de IA también muestra una gran afinidad entre los usuarios de más de 35 años. En el mercado del Reino Unido, la representación de los usuarios de Wondershare.com de 35 años en adelante es 1.26 veces mayor (126) que su representación en la población digital total del país, seguido de cerca por los visitantes únicos de la misma edad en México (104). En 2023, la IA generativa ha conseguido hacerse un hueco en nuestra manera de escribir, editar y diseñar, transformando así la creación de contenido, especialmente entre los jóvenes. Con la evolución de esta tecnología, es probable que cada vez más personas utilicen estas herramientas en los próximos años. Para obtener más información sobre la audiencia de estas u otras plataformas digitales, contacta a tu representante de Comscore o escríbenos a través de comscore.com/learnmore Definiciones: * El índice de composición de visitantes únicos/UV compara la proporción de un perfil de visitante único en un sitio web dado, con la proporción de este mismo perfil en el total Internet. Por ejemplo, si un perfil de un visitante único corresponde al 20% de la audiencia de un sitio web pero al 10% de todos los usuarios de Internet, entonces el índice de composición UV = 20% / 10% x 100 = 200. title: Long-Context Isn't the Answer
summary: We tried Opus with 1M context for coding agents, and now we're switching back. It turns out it's not about the size of the context window - it's about the quality.
body_text: Anthropic just switched the default model in Claude Code to Opus 4.6 with a 1M context window. We tried it when it launched. But now we're switching back to Opus 4.5 ## How about some context? Unlike previous Claude Opus models which have a ~ 200k context window, Opus 4.6 has as 1M context window. This was very exciting for us! We spend a lot of time working on hard problems in large enterprise codebases, and if the model can reliably hold more of the codebase in its head at a time, so to speak, then that creates new possibilities for the scale of problem that can be solved in a single context window. It would mean less compaction (whether frequent intentional compaction or auto-compact), and less "context pressure" to solve the problem before your context window fills up. As Calvin French-Owen, who helped launch Codex last year, puts it in an episode of YC's Lightcone podcast : ...imagine you're a college student. You're taking an exam. In the first five minutes of that exam, you're like, "Oh, I have all the time in the world. I'll do a great job. I'll think through each of these problems." Let's say you have like five minutes left and you still have half the exam left. You're like, "Oh man, I just got to do whatever I can." Like, that's the LLM with a context window ## More context, less instruction adherence While the context window is dramatically larger, we noticed over the course of a couple of weeks that instruction adherence was dramatically degraded, and not just at longer context lengths. Even well-within what we would consider the smart zone of a 200k-context frontier model, the model was less precise. It would ignore design documents and other inputs when writing a plan file. It would make trivial mistakes, or misunderstand simple instructions - or worse, directly disobey them. At longer context lengths, the degradation was even steeper - like the user instructions were getting drowned out by the intermediate tool results and mass of accumulated context. ## What determines instruction adherence? We've written about the concept of the instruction budget before - a measurable property of LLMs which describes how many instructions they can follow reasonably well before instruction adherence drops off. It's different for each model, but it's a function primarily of the quality of the model's instruction tuning, and more importantly for our purposes, it is strongly correlated with the size of the model . You can clearly see that the larger models from the study can follow dramatically more instructions before adherence drops off. ## Instruction adherence at long context lengths Why does this matter? When a lab offers an extended-context version of a model, you're usually not getting a bigger model with more parameters and therefore a larger "instruction budget" to go with the larger context window - you're likely getting the same model with some clever math (e.g. YaRN ) to extend the sequence length the model can attend to, and probably some more post-training to stabilize the model at the longer sequence lengths. This means that while the context window size increases, the instruction budget remains the same. You can fit more context and more instructions in the context window, but the model isn't actually better at attending to those instructions over the context length. ## Instruction-following as needle in a haystack You can think of your context window as a haystack where all of your tool calls and documents and files are hay - every line in your CLAUDE.md file, every instruction in your tool descriptions, every tool result, every instruction in your system prompt, and every user message. The quality & correctness of the agent's next step depends on the LLM's ability to find a needle in there: namely, the instruction(s) in the context window that are most-relevant to the current state of the context window, which give it the information it needs to make the correct decision about its next action. Now imagine we increase the size of the haystack by 500% - but the size of the needle remains the same. Unless our ability to find the needle also increases by 500%, we will have a dramatically harder time finding it. The extra context isn't really helping us - it's just digging us deeper into the dumb zone. ## What Works Instead Instead of trying to stuff as much information in a context window as possible and having the LLM reason over it, we found that the context management techniques we had been using had to be used even more aggressively to keep Opus 4.6 1M on track. In my post on harness engineering , I wrote about this as the limit case for using sub-agents: The day after I published it, I decided maybe it wasn't such a bad idea, and sat down and wrote this skill: --- name: subagent-orchestrator description: orchestrate sub-agents to accomplish complex long-horizon tasks without losing coherency by delegating to sub-agents --- This skill provides you with **CRITICAL** instructions that will help you to maintain coherency in long-horizon context-heavy tasks. You have a large number of tools available to you. The most important one is the one that allows you to dispatch sub-agents: either `Agent` or `Task`. All non-trivial operations should be delegated to sub-agents. You should delegate research and codebase understanding tasks to codebase-analyzer, codebase-locator and pattern-locator sub-agents. You should delegate running bash commands (particularly ones that are likely to produce lots of output) such as investigating with the `aws` CLI, using the `gh` CLI, digging through logs to `Bash` sub-agents. You should use separate sub-agents for separate tasks, and you may launch them in parallel - but do not delegate multiple tasks that are likely to have significant overlap to separate sub-agents. IMPORTANT: if the user has already given you a task, you should proceed with that task using this approach. If you have not already been explicitly given a taks, you should ask the user what task they would like for you to work on - do not assume or begin working on a ticket automatically. I found that using this skill in combination with our existing workflow skills helped me keep Opus coherent at longer context lengths. Why? As I wrote about in that post, sub-agents encapsulate context and ensure that only highly-relevant context (the prompt, and the focused sub-agent result) end up in the context window, avoiding context rot : ## How we're incorporating this at HumanLayer We have had a feature in the tool for a while that warns the user when they're context is getting high. We used to set this at around %40 of sonnets 168k token window (200k - 32k reserved for output). This came out to about 100k tokens. To help users maximize instruction adherence and intelligence on hard codebase problems, we've updated our context warnings for long-context models to trigger at the 100k token mark instead of 40% of the usable context. For opus 1m this is only 10% of the context window. ## TL;DR Long-context models degrade at all context lengths, not just long ones. More context isn't more capability - the instruction budget doesn't scale with the context window. Context isolation beats context expansion. Sub-agents, progressive disclosure, and context-efficient backpressure keep each context window small, focused, and in the smart zone.

title: Iron Condor Strategy Explained: How It Works, Payoff & Example
summary: Discover when to use the Iron Condor strategy, how to calculate profit and loss, manage risk, and backtest your trades before going live.
body_text: Iron Condor Strategy Explained: How It Works, Payoff & Example AlgoTest Jul 22, 2026 • 7 min read • Strategies • Markdown Twitter / X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Ask ChatGPT Ask Claude Ask Grok Copy link What Is an Iron Condor Strategy? An iron condor strategy is a four-leg, market-neutral options strategy that combines a bear call spread and a bull put spread on the same underlying and expiry. It profits when the underlying stays within a defined price range until expiry, making it a popular choice for traders expecting sideways market movement. The strategy is opened for a net credit by selling one out-of-the-money (OTM) call and one OTM put, while buying a further OTM call and put to cap risk on both sides. The credit received is the maximum possible profit, which you keep if the underlying closes between the two short strikes at expiry. This version, where the nearer strikes are sold and the farther strikes are bought for protection, is known as the short iron condor and is the variation most options traders use. (A long iron condor is a less common debit strategy built in the opposite direction.) Let's see how the iron condor strategy works, its payoff, when to use it, how to choose strikes, and how to build and backtest one on AlgoTest. How the Iron Condor Is Structured Sell one OTM call above the current price to collect premium on the upside. Buy one further OTM call above your short call to cap your upside risk. Sell one OTM put below the current price to collect premium on the downside. Buy one further OTM put below your short put to cap your downside risk. All four legs share the same expiry date, and the position is usually opened as a single combined order rather than four separate trades. You can learn more about ATM, ITM, OTM here. Iron Condor Payoff The payoff on an iron condor is defined and capped on both sides, and you can work it out before you ever place the trade. Maximum Profit: Net premium (credit) received when you open the position. You keep this in full if the underlying closes between your two short strikes at expiry. Maximum Loss: Width of either spread minus the net premium received. Both spreads are usually kept equal in width, so this figure holds on either side. Breakeven Points Upper breakeven: Short call strike + net credit Lower breakeven: Short put strike − net credit Iron Condor Example on Nifty Example: Nifty at 24,500, weekly expiry Sell the 24,700 CE and the 24,300 PE Buy the 24,900 CE and the 24,100 PE Net credit received: Rs. 45 per share With a Nifty lot size of 65: Maximum profit: Rs. 2,925 (45 x 65), if Nifty closes between 24,300 and 24,700 Maximum loss: Rs. 10,075 (155 x 65), if Nifty closes beyond 24,100 or 24,900 Upper breakeven: 24,745 | Lower breakeven: 24,255 Numbers are illustrative, not a trade recommendation. When to Use an Iron Condor The underlying has been trading in a well-defined range with no clear trend. You expect the market to stay range-bound rather than make a strong directional move, since that's what determines whether your short strikes hold, not the VIX level on its own. Many traders prefer opening an iron condor when implied volatility is relatively high compared to its recent levels, since that means richer premiums for the same strike distance. Low IV can still work, but it also means less credit for the risk you're taking on. No major scheduled events fall within the trade's holding period, such as an RBI policy announcement, the Union Budget, or a heavyweight earnings release. You want defined, capped risk instead of the open-ended exposure that comes with naked option selling. Related: Option Trading Strategies When Not to Use an Iron Condor A major scheduled event, such as RBI policy, the Union Budget, or a big earnings release, falls inside your holding period. Implied volatility is expected to expand sharply rather than stay flat or contract. The underlying is trending strongly in one direction rather than moving sideways. A breakout is already underway by the time you're looking to enter. The options you'd need to trade have poor liquidity, which widens your entry and exit costs on all four legs. Related: Mistakes Traders make in Algo trading Strike Selection and Risk Management Many traders anchor their short strikes using delta as a proxy for probability, commonly placing the short call and put in the 20 to 30 delta range so each side has a reasonable statistical chance of expiring worthless. Some traders use the expected move, nearby support and resistance levels, or implied volatility instead of delta alone when picking strikes, especially around events where delta-based probabilities can be misleading. Wider wings (the distance between your short and long strikes) increase your credit and your maximum loss together, so widen them in proportion to how much risk you're comfortable holding, not just to chase a bigger premium. Keep your two spreads symmetric unless you have a mild directional view, since a heavily skewed iron condor starts to behave more like a single credit spread with extra legs. Size the position against the margin it blocks, not just the premium it pays, so you have room left to adjust if the market moves against one side. Adjusting an Iron Condor Position Roll the untested side closer to the current price to collect additional credit if one side of the range is clearly safe and the other is under pressure. Close the position early once you've captured a large share of the maximum profit, since the remaining credit often isn't worth the residual risk of holding to expiry. Exit or reduce the threatened side if the underlying approaches your short strike well before expiry, rather than waiting for the breakeven point to be tested. Avoid adjusting reactively on every small move. Decide your adjustment triggers before you enter the trade so you're not making risk decisions in the middle of a fast market. Iron Condor vs Iron Butterfly An iron condor sells out-of-the-money strikes, which gives it a wider profit range but a smaller credit. An iron butterfly (also called an iron fly) sells at-the-money strikes instead, which means a narrower profit zone but a larger credit for the same risk taken. Feature Iron Condor Iron Butterfly Short strikes OTM ATM Credit received Lower Higher Profit range Wider Narrower Risk Defined Defined Best suited for Mildly range-bound markets Tightly range-bound markets In practice, traders reach for an iron condor when they expect the underlying to stay within a broader range, and an iron butterfly when they have a more precise view on where it will settle. If you want the full breakdown of strike selection and payoff mechanics for the butterfly side, AlgoTest's butterfly option strategy guide covers that in detail. Common Mistakes to Avoid Setting your range too tight relative to the underlying's realistic movement, which increases the odds of a breach before expiry. Ignoring scheduled events like RBI policy days, Budget day, or major earnings that fall inside your holding period. Entering the trade without a predefined adjustment plan, which tends to turn small losses into large ones. Oversizing the position relative to available capital, leaving no room to adjust the threatened side if the market moves. Holding an untouched position all the way into expiry day without accounting for how fast gamma risk builds up in the final session. How to Build and Backtest an Iron Condor with AlgoTest Constructing an iron condor by hand across four legs leaves room for error, especially when you're trying to keep both spreads symmetric and track combined margin in real time. AlgoTest's Strategy Builder lets you add all four legs from the option chain, see the combined payoff graph, Greeks, and margin requirement as you build, and adjust strikes before you commit capital. Pre-built Iron Condor template in AlgoTest Strategy Builder Once the structure is set, you can backtest this iron condor trading strategy against historical data to see how it would have performed across different market conditions, then paper trade it before going live. For a step-by-step walkthrough of building a monthly iron condor in the Strategy Builder, see How to Use AlgoTest Strategy Builder for a Monthly Iron Condor . If you trade shorter timeframes, Intraday Iron Condor Built Using Straddle Width shows how to size your wings using the day's straddle price instead of fixed points. Trade Iron Condors With More Confidence An iron condor strategy can be an effective way to generate income in range-bound markets while keeping risk defined. Success, however, depends less on the strategy itself and more on choosing the right strikes, sizing positions appropriately, and having a clear exit or adjustment plan. Before trading with real capital, test your setup using historical data and paper trading. With AlgoTest's Strategy Builder, you can build, backtest, and refine your iron condor strategy to evaluate different strike combinations and adjustment rules before taking it live. As the industry moves beyond proof of concept toward value, deployment, and commercialization, MicroVision delivers integrated hardware and software solutions designed for real-world performance, automotive-grade reliability, and economic scalability. With engineering centers in the U.S. and Germany, MicroVision leads the industry in depth and breadth of its portfolio, with both short- and long-range lidar solutions, featuring solid-state sensors with varying wavelengths, advanced sensor architectures, design-to-cost engineering, and open software solutions. title: Propexo CEO Featured in Article Discussing Impact of RealPage Lawsuit
summary: Remen Okoruwa predicts increased constraints on data sharing that will hinder innovation
body_text: Remen Okoruwa, Co-Founder and CEO of Propexo, recently shared insights with Multifamily Dive on how the Department of Justice's antitrust lawsuit against RealPage is reshaping data sharing practices in the multifamily industry. In the article, Okoruwa highlighted a significant shift in data processing agreements, noting that major REITs are now implementing stricter vendor policies that prohibit data aggregation beyond specified purposes. Okoruwa predicted this trend will continue, observing that "everyone's looking at what's happening to RealPage, and it's really clear that this will change things," while emphasizing the industry's need for clearer guidelines around permissible data sharing practices. He also raised concerns about potential broader implications beyond pricing data, suggesting that other forms of data sharing could face similar scrutiny. You can read the full analysis at Multifamily Dive .

title: How to Make Longer AI Videos: A Practical Guide for 2026
summary: To make longer AI videos, start from a structured document or chaptered outline, use a document-to-video tool like Knowlify instead of short clip generators, and build by section so length comes from content, not padding.
body_text: Step 2: Build a chaptered source document Longer AI video lives or dies on structure. Before you generate, create or clean a source file with: A title and one-sentence goal H2-style chapter headings (one idea per section) Short paragraphs written for the ear, not for a policy binder Optional speaker notes or bullets under each heading A closing CTA or knowledge check PDF, PowerPoint, Google Docs, and Word all work. For a deeper walkthrough of that pipeline, see how document-to-video works and the PDF to video guide . A 2,000-word blob with no headings will produce a mushy long video. The same content with five clear chapters will produce a watchable one. Step 3: Generate in Knowlify from the document Upload the document (or paste a structured prompt) into the Knowlify platform or the explainer video maker . Knowlify reads the structure, drafts a script and storyboard, generates animated scenes, and adds narration. You are not assembling a timeline from scratch. For longer projects, prefer one of these patterns: One document, one video when chapters already flow as a single lesson One document per chapter, then a playlist when completion rates matter more than a single file Studio delivery when you want a polished multi-minute piece without editing every scene yourself CMS Vocational Training used Knowlify to ship 241 videos in 6 weeks , with videos averaging around five minutes. That is the opposite of the 8-second clip workflow, and it is the pattern most L&D and enablement teams actually need. Step 4: Extend length with content, not filler If the draft is shorter than your target, do not ask the model to "make it longer" in the abstract. Add substance: Expand a thin chapter in the source doc, then regenerate Add a worked example, checklist, or common mistake section Insert a short demo of the workflow the viewer must follow Add a recap and clear next step at the end In Knowlify, refine with plain-language edits ("add a 30-second example after chapter 2," "slow the narration in the safety steps," "split scene 4 into two scenes"). Chat edits beat remaking the whole project. If the draft is too long, cut a chapter into its own video. A series of focused modules almost always beats one bloated file for training completion. Pair this guide with scriptwriting for training videos when the narration feels dense. Step 5: Review for long-form retention Longer video needs a different QA pass than a 60-second explainer. Does the first 15 seconds say what the viewer will learn? Does each chapter earn the next minute? Are transitions obvious when the topic changes? Is the CTA or knowledge check easy to find at the end? Would a busy employee finish this in one sitting? Export the MP4, drop it in your LMS, help center, or YouTube, and watch analytics. Drop-off after a specific chapter usually means that chapter should become its own video, not that AI "cannot do long form." Start free on Knowlify with a chaptered doc, or book a demo if you want Studio to produce the longer piece for you. Tips That Keep Longer AI Videos Watchable Front-load the promise. Tell viewers the chapters up front. Longer videos without a map feel endless. One idea per scene. Dense slides become dense scenes. Split them. Write for speech. Read the script out loud. If you run out of breath, the sentence is too long. Use brand once, then stay consistent. Logo, colors, and style should not reset every chapter. Prefer a series when attention is cold. Marketing audiences rarely want 10 minutes. Learners and subscribers often will. Update the doc, regenerate the video. Document-to-video keeps long training libraries maintainable. That is harder with stitched clip tools. Key Takeaways Longer AI video is a workflow problem more than a prompt problem. Short clip tools are the wrong category for multi-minute business content. Structure the source: chapters, headings, and speech-friendly copy. Knowlify is a strong fit because document-to-video scales with content length, not clip duration. Add length by adding useful sections, not by asking the model to pad. Split into a series when completion matters more than a single long file. Use Studio when you want a polished longer video without owning every edit. FAQ How to make longer AI videos? Start with a chaptered document or outline, then use a document-to-video tool such as Knowlify instead of a short clip generator. Generate the video from that structure, expand thin sections in the source doc when you need more runtime, and refine scenes with plain-language edits. For polished delivery without DIY editing, use Knowlify Studio . How do I make a long AI video? Write or upload a structured source (headings, chapters, examples), set a target length that matches the use case, and generate with a tool built for narrated multi-scene video. Knowlify turns PDFs, decks, and docs into longer explainers and training videos. Avoid tools that only output a few seconds per prompt if your goal is several minutes. How can I make AI videos longer than 1 minute? Most sub-minute limits come from clip-style generators. Switch to document-to-video or a full AI video maker that supports multi-scene scripts. In Knowlify, a multi-page doc or multi-section deck naturally produces a video longer than a minute because length follows the source content. How do I make a 5 minute AI video? Outline five chapters that each take about a minute of narration (roughly 130 to 150 spoken words per minute). Put that outline in a document, generate in Knowlify, then add examples where a chapter feels thin. Review pacing so each minute still teaches something concrete. How do I make a 10 minute AI video? Treat it as a short lesson, not a stretched promo. Use a clear agenda, chapter titles on screen, and a mid-point recap. Generate from a longer source doc in Knowlify, or split into two 5-minute modules if your LMS completion data drops on long videos. Studio can also deliver a finished 10-minute piece when you want less hands-on editing. Why are AI videos so short? Many popular AI video products optimize for social clips and image-to-video shots that only sustain a few seconds of continuity. Business video needs script structure, scene planning, and narration across many beats. Document-to-video platforms are designed for that longer arc. What is the best AI video generator for long videos? For business training, onboarding, and explainers, pick a tool that starts from documents and supports multi-scene narration. Knowlify is a strong option because it converts existing PDFs, PowerPoint, Google Docs, and Word files into animated, narrated video, and Studio can deliver longer finished videos for you. Clip-first tools are usually a poor fit past a minute. How do I extend AI video length without making it boring? Add useful content: examples, checklists, demos, FAQs, and a recap. Do not ask the model to "make it longer" with filler adjectives. If a section does not teach a new step, cut it or move it to another video. Can AI make long form videos? Yes, when you use the right category of tool and a structured brief. AI can draft scripts, scenes, and voiceover for multi-minute videos. Quality still depends on your outline, source accuracy, and review pass. Knowlify is built for that longer, document-driven workflow. How do I make longer text to video outputs? Replace a one-line prompt with a full outline or paste the full article or script into a document-to-video or text-to-video workflow that accepts long input. See our text-to-video AI guide for prompt-based tools, and prefer document upload in Knowlify when you already have the content written. How do I stitch AI video clips into one longer video? You can export clips and join them in a traditional editor, but that is usually the slow path. A cleaner approach is to generate one multi-scene project from a single structured document so transitions, voice, and brand stay consistent. Use stitching only when you must combine outputs from different tools. Should I make one long AI video or a series of short ones? Use one longer video when the audience is motivated and the topic is one continuous lesson. Use a series when topics can stand alone, when completion rates matter, or when people will revisit a single section later. Microlearning teams usually win with a series. Details live in our microlearning guide . How long should an AI explainer video be? For cold marketing audiences, 60 to 90 seconds is still the sweet spot. For training and onboarding, several minutes can be right. Length should follow the job. See the explainer video length guide for benchmarks by purpose and platform. How do I make a longer explainer video with AI? Define one core message, expand it into chapters (problem, how it works, proof, next step), put that into a doc, and generate with Knowlify. Keep marketing explainers lean. Reserve longer runtime for demos, tutorials, and education. For the classic short explainer process, see how to make an explainer video . Does Knowlify support longer AI videos? Yes. Knowlify is designed for narrated, multi-scene business video from real documents, not just short social clips. Teams use it for multi-minute training and learning content, including high-volume programs like the CMS Vocational Training case study . Start free or book a demo to see a longer workflow on your own material. For Indian teams hiring proactively, Weekday delivers interested candidates to your calendar faster than any other platform. Stop waiting for the best talent to apply. FAQs About HR AI Tools in India What are the best AI tools for HR in India? The best HR AI tools for Indian teams depend on use case. Weekday leads for proactive recruiting and passive candidate sourcing with 300M+ profiles and automated WhatsApp, email, and phone outreach. Darwinbox and Keka are strong for enterprise and mid-market HRMS with payroll compliance. greytHR and sumHR serve SMBs needing affordable payroll automation. Eightfold AI and SAP SuccessFactors provide enterprise talent intelligence and analytics. Leapsome excels at AI-powered performance management. Indian HR teams typically layer a recruiting specialist like Weekday with an HRMS platform for payroll and compliance. How is AI used in HR and recruitment in India? AI-enabled HR systems have helped reduce average time-to-hire by 23 percent in India. AI automates resume screening, ranks candidates by fit and intent, sources passive talent from databases, predicts attrition risk 60-90 days before departure, generates performance insights, and handles multi-channel outreach via email, WhatsApp, and phone. Modern AI tools handle coordination loops automatically, verify documents via Digilocker, and schedule interviews. Weekday uses AI to surface passive candidates from India's largest professional database, draft personalized outreach messages, and automate follow-ups until candidates respond. What is the ROI of HR AI tools for Indian companies? Total HR AI program ROI targets for Indian mid-market firms range from Rs 150 to 160 lakh annual savings against Rs 15 to 18 lakh investment. Automated payroll processing can save processing time by 25%. India's attrition rate fell to 13.6% in 2026 from 17.1% in 2025, but sector variation is extreme (e-commerce leads at 28.7%, IT averages 25%). AI-driven attrition prediction and proactive retention reduce replacement hiring costs. Weekday 's proactive sourcing delivers 50%+ response rates and ~50% fill rates, cutting agency fees and time-to-hire for critical roles. Why do Indian HR teams need WhatsApp integration? India runs on WhatsApp. Mid and senior hiring in India has specific requirements including passive talent discovery, anonymous candidate profiles, intent prediction, and India-specific compliance. Passive candidates earning Rs 15 LPA+ rarely check email daily but respond to WhatsApp instantly. Weekday integrates native WhatsApp outreach alongside email and phone, delivering response rates 50%+ higher than email-only platforms. Multi-channel outreach is not optional in India (it is how you reach the candidates who matter). Are AI recruiting tools biased in India? A Stanford study from 2025 found that some AI-driven resume screening tools consistently rated older male candidates higher than equally qualified female and younger applicants. For Indian organizations navigating diversity mandates and building more inclusive workplaces, the lesson is clear: AI should assist hiring decisions, not automate them without oversight. Look for platforms with transparent matching algorithms, audit trails, and the ability to exclude demographic signals (name, gender, age, university) from scoring. Weekday 's smart filters focus on skills, experience, and intent (not proxies for bias). What HR compliance challenges do AI tools solve in India? A 2023 KPMG India benchmark found mid-market firms lose around 30% of HR Ops time to manual payroll rectification. AI payroll platforms auto-calculate PF, ESI, PT (which varies by state), and TDS, flag compliance deadlines, generate Form 16s, and update automatically when slabs change. sumHR is one of the best attendance and payroll software in India that takes care of everything, from tax liabilities to payroll operations, allowing businesses to manage ESI, professional tax, salaries, TDS, and much more. This reduces compliance risk, penalty exposure, and manual rectification workload. How do I choose between Weekday, Darwinbox, and Keka? Pick Weekday if your primary challenge is finding and engaging passive candidates for mid-to-senior roles. Weekday is the only platform built for proactive, outbound hiring in India with 300M+ profiles and multi-channel outreach. Pick Darwinbox if you are a 1,000+ employee enterprise needing deep performance management, multi-entity payroll, and audit-grade compliance controls. Pick Keka if you are a 200-800 employee mid-market firm wanting clean UI, transparent pricing, and solid payroll automation without enterprise complexity. Most high-growth Indian companies layer Weekday (for recruiting) with Keka or Darwinbox (for HRMS and payroll). What is the difference between AI recruiting tools and HRMS platforms? AI recruiting tools like Weekday, Eightfold AI, and hireEZ focus on sourcing, screening, and engaging candidates (solving the top-of-funnel talent acquisition challenge). HRMS platforms like Darwinbox, Keka, greytHR, and Zoho People manage employee lifecycle post-hire: payroll, attendance, leave, performance, and compliance. Unlike traditional ATS systems, which primarily focus on tracking applicants through the hiring funnel, talent intelligence platforms provide a holistic approach to talent acquisition and management. Indian HR teams typically need both: a recruiting specialist to fill roles proactively and an HRMS to manage employees compliantly.
